The most worthwhile change is inside the existing expanded task row. In the same comparison panel, the current editor scored 5.50/10. Wrapping both dates onto a second line scored 7.83. Naming the fields within that space scored 9.50 from all three reviewers. Both versions keep the original card, Notes field, completion circle and next task in position.

Compact · 8.78/10. Keep the deadline at the trailing edge, spell out Today, darken the small scheduled date, and add a single check in the workspace menu. This keeps the collapsed rows especially quiet. All three reviewers still had to look across the row to connect the deadline with its title.

Descriptive · 9.56/10. Put Due today directly beneath the title, label the date pills, distinguish Tuesday and Thursday in the month grid, and connect Today to the selected Planner menu item. The project-list difference was small: 8.50 versus 8.33 for Compact. “No schedule” spends gutter space on every undated row. A named editor field earned a much clearer benefit.

The initial baseline was 8.28. The identical current screenshots scored 7.47 when mixed with the candidates. Relative to that repeat control, Compact gained 1.31 points and Descriptive gained 2.08 points, calculated before rounding. Treat these as panel judgments on the six pictured states. All three reviewers still found the Notes placeholder pale in the higher-scoring editor.

How the reviewers scored

Three fresh, independent iPhone UI reviewers scored the six current screens first. Three different reviewers then scored 18 unnamed, shuffled images, including an exact repeat of each current screen. All used Codex GPT-6.2-astra with high reasoning effort. Each reviewer rated orientation, scanability, affordance, legibility and composition from 0 to 2 in half-point steps. Summing the five marks gave a score out of ten. Each screen and reviewer counted equally. The two phases used the same brief. The half-point anchors are new to this study.

Native screenshots came from the two passing XCUITests at revision 4fe70da. For both concepts the full-resolution screenshot forms the background. Localized text and SF Symbol overlays are rendered at 3× in headless Chrome on macOS. Pixel comparison verified an exact match between every rendered control screenshot and its native source, with under 1% of RGB pixels changed in each candidate. The overlays establish visual fit at this viewport. Only the app build provides evidence for native layout, scrolling, gestures and Dynamic Type.

The footer dash outside Planner is intentional. The existing app uses it to open the month picker and supports a long press to return to Today. Both candidates preserve it despite reviewer uncertainty about its meaning. Planner design history · Baseline XCUITest evidence
